# Managing an open trade

## The answer
Hold a runner only after the first target is banked. Trim into strength, then trail the rest behind a rising floor. ([[Notes/module-1/lesson-1.2|1.2]], [[Notes/module-2/lesson-2.1|2.1]])

## How it works

### Trimming
- Sell a third at the first target and move the protective line to breakeven. ([[Notes/module-1/lesson-1.2|1.2]])
- Keep a small runner so one good move can pay for several scratches. ([[Notes/module-2/lesson-2.1|2.1]])

### Trailing a runner
- Trail the runner behind each higher low; exit when the floor breaks. ([[Notes/module-2/lesson-2.1|2.1]])
- Do not widen the line once the runner is open. ([[Notes/module-3.1/lesson-3.1.1|3.1.1]])

## Where lessons disagree
- One lesson trims half, another trims a third. ([[Notes/module-1/lesson-1.2|1.2]])

## Small-account and 0DTE notes
- With a small account keep the runner tiny and bank the first target quickly.

## What the course doesn't cover
- Nothing on tax treatment of gains.
